Armed Conflict & Security

Why it matters: Escalating regional hostilities, accountability for mass violence, and military readiness issues are shaping security dynamics from the Middle East to North America.

The Kingdom stresses the importance of an immediate halt to the blatant Iranian attacks on the countries of the region, and of taking serious steps towards achieving security and stability for the countries of the region and their peoples.The continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts to contain the tension and undermine political and diplomatic endeavors aimed at achieving security and stability in the region.The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s strongest condemnation of the continued Iranian aggression against its territory, including the attack launched today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, by drones that were intercepted and destroyed by air defense systems in the Kingdom’s airspace.This comes two days after a similar attack at dawn on Friday, November 13, 2026, by two drones that were also intercepted. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard explicitly claimed responsibility for these attacks. The Ministry praised the efficiency, vigilance, and capability of the Bahrain Defense Force in confronting today’s attack and its complete readiness to deter any aggression.

Economy & Markets.title: Can America’s Next Jobs Boom Build a Middle-Class Life?
Economy & Markets.text: America’s aging population is driving rapid growth in demand for home care workers, but many of those jobs still offer wages too low to support a family. Ai-jen Poo of the National Domestic Workers Alliance says the country will need hundreds of thousands of additional home care workers in the coming decades, while Harvard economist Lawrence Katz argues that expanding the workforce will not be enough if those jobs offer little opportunity for workers to move up. The challenge is whether care work can follow the path of manufacturing and evolve from low-wage labor into a stable route to the middle class. (Source: Bloomberg)

Entertainment.text: SummaryLeica releases the M-A and M11-P cameras featuring a rare, vintage hammertone finish.The analog and digital models pair textured solid brass with vulcanite-style leatherette.Available worldwide, the premium cameras retail for approx. $7,100 - $10,100 USD, respectively.Leica is reviving one of the rarest finishes in its archive with the M-A Hammertone and M11-P Hammertone, two special-edition rangefinders that wrap their top and base plates in a textured, mottled coating. The finish dates back to the 1930s and became shorthand in German industrial design for toughness and dependability, with its signature pattern forming as the coating dries and metallic pigments and additives create slight shifts in surface tension.On Leica bodies it has appeared only sporadically, from the Leica MD documentation camera built for the Leitz Reprovit system to a 1964 Leica MD produced in a run of just ten, followed by later releases such as the 2003 MP LHSA, the 2011 M9 Hammertone and the 2016 M-A Vienna Edition. For this pair, Leica reworked the process, relying on specialists at its Wetzlar Manufacture to achieve an even result across the texture, and since the surface never forms the same way twice, each camera ends up one of a kind. The solid brass bodies combine that finish with cross-knurled controls, a polished silver shutter-release plate and black vulcanite-style leatherette with white engravings, while the M11-P Hammertone adds softer, rounded edges on its top and base plates and a silver-chrome front screw.Beneath the vintage-industrial look, both cameras mirror their standard counterparts. The M-A Hammertone is a fully mechanical film camera built for purists, with aperture, shutter speed and film sensitivity all set by hand. The M11-P Hammertone carries the same aesthetic into Leica's digital M-System, featuring Leica Content Credentials for verifiable authorship and editing history, 256 GB of internal storage, a scratch-resistant sapphire-crystal screen, a full-frame BSI CMOS sensor with Triple Resolution Technology shooting at 60, 36 or 18 megapixels, and Leica FOTOS App connectivity via Bluetooth, Wi-Fi or cable, along with a BP-SCL7 battery finished to match.Both editions are now available through Leica and its authorized dealers, with the M-A Hammertone priced at £5,700 GBP (approx. $7,600 USD) and the M11-P Hammertone at £8,500 GBP (approx. $11,300 USD). Additional hammertone BP-SCL7 batteries are available for £160 GBP (approx. $215 USD).Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: KidSuper and Mercedes-Benz Have Football Fever
Entertainment.text: SummaryKidSuper and Mercedes-Benz celebrate seven World Cup-winning nations with a 17-piece collection connecting football and automotive history.The collection pairs iconic Mercedes-Benz vehicles with national team colors, historic victories, and football-inspired designs.Priced from $125 to $595 USD, the collection launches November 14 alongside a special event at KidSuper Studios in Brooklyn.KidSuper and Mercedes-Benz are bringing football history to the forefront of their latest collaboration. First previewed during KidSuper's Spring/Summer 2027 runway show in Miami, the collection celebrates seven World Cup-winning nations by pairing their football heritage with iconic Mercedes-Benz vehicles.Marking 140 years of Mercedes-Benz, the collaboration takes inspiration from the stars found above national team crests, each representing a World Cup victory. For KidSuper founder Colm Dillane, the symbol serves as a connection between generations of football fans, with each country's sporting achievements paired with a Mercedes-Benz model from a corresponding era.Spanning 17 pieces, the collection brings together football jerseys, tracksuits, tailoring, knitwear, and accessories, incorporating national colors, historic dates, and automotive references throughout.Brazil's football legacy is reimagined through a tailored jacket inspired by the Mercedes-Benz 220 SE, while Uruguay's history informs a navy crochet polo referencing the SSK. Germany's 300 SL Coupé appears on a black zip-up jacket, while Argentina's 450 SEL 6.9 inspires a printed shirt and leather-trimmed bag.Elsewhere, France's G 500 is referenced through a blue workwear set, Spain's SLS AMG Coupé Electric Drive Concept inspires a colorful football jersey, and England's Mercedes-Benz 600 is translated into a burgundy tracksuit.Throughout the collection, KidSuper reworks the Mercedes-Benz three-pointed star alongside football iconography, combining the visual language of vintage sportswear, automotive memorabilia, and national team merchandise.The KidSuper x Mercedes-Benz collection is available from today, with prices ranging from $125 USD to $595 USD. Available in store and online at KidSuper, alongside select global retailers, the release will also be celebrated with a public event at KidSuper Studios in Williamsburg, featuring a display of Mercedes-Benz vehicles, music, food, and drinks.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Siegelman Stable's Holiday Homecoming Takes Over SoHo
Entertainment.text: SummarySiegelman Stable returns to SoHo for the holidays with a six-week pop-up featuring exclusive drops, coveted restocks, and its FW26 collection.The space features an Almost Home coffee bar, lounge, and interiors inspired by the late 1980s.In partnership with Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business, the brand will host special events and programming for New York's entrepreneurial community.Siegelman Stable is back in New York City for the holidays. Following previous pop-ups in SoHo, East Hampton, and Chicago, the brand returns to its hometown with a new retail space at 430 W Broadway, open through December 23.Presented in partnership with Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business, the holiday pop-up will feature exclusive releases, restocks of some of the brand's most sought-after pieces, and its latest Fall/Winter 2026 collection. While Siegelman Stable has become known for its signature headwear, the space will also highlight its growing ready-to-wear offering, including an expanded selection of knitwear.Designed by ForEveryday.Life alongside creative director Karoline Spenning, the store takes inspiration from the late 1980s, with rich blue walls, velvet curtains, suede finishes, and plush carpeting. An Almost Home coffee bar and lounge at the back of the space offer visitors somewhere to unwind between shopping.Beyond retail, Siegelman Stable is making room for New York's entrepreneurial community. Throughout the pop-up, the brand and Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business will host special programming, including a founder's roundtable focused on navigating the holiday season as a business owner, alongside dedicated early shopping hours."We've had our biggest growth year to date, and now we have to pop up at home in NYC and show who we are as a brand in person," said founder Max Siegelman, emphasizing the importance of creating physical experiences as the brand continues to grow.Siegelman Stable's holiday pop-up is now open at 430 W Broadway in SoHo through December 23, with prices ranging from $38 USD to $2,200 USD. Climate & Environment.text: Two centuries after the expedition, Indigenous students are conducting a new wildlife survey along the routeIn 1804, when Thomas Jefferson dispatched Meriwether Lewis and William Clark and their Corps of Discovery to explore the newly acquired land west of the Mississippi, the president’s primary aim was political: Americans needed to establish presence, power and trade routes in these territories before the Europeans beat them to it.But Jefferson, an ardent naturalist, had a secondary agenda. He ordered that the expedition also survey the flora and fauna of these landscapes. On their two-year jaunt across the western half of the country, Lewis and Clark kept meticulous journals of the animals and plants they encountered: bison, horned lizards, sage grouse, prairie dogs, wild licorice and catfish, among them. Art & Culture.title: Kengo Kuma’s KAI Water Culture House Is Built From Roughly 300,000 Handmade Bricks
Art & Culture.text: SummaryKengo Kuma & Associates unveils Copenhagen's 5,800-square-meter KAI Water Culture House.The complex features handmade brick towers above a glazed base.Opening December 5, it offers ten pools and wellness facilities.Kengo Kuma & Associates, in collaboration with Cornelius Vöge Atelier for Architecture and Vilhelm Lauritzen Architects, has announced the upcoming opening of the KAI Water Culture House in Copenhagen, Denmark. Set to officially open to the public on December 5, 2026, the expansive 5,800-square-meter facility is situated prominently on Papirøen (Paper Island).Conceived as a major public waterfront destination, the monumental complex seamlessly combines ten distinct indoor and outdoor pools, comprehensive wellness facilities and versatile cultural spaces to establish a dynamic new focal point for recreation and community gathering within the city's rapidly transforming harbor. The project’s roots stretch back nearly a decade: in 2015, the City of Copenhagen asked residents to pitch ideas for a cultural and leisure venue on the island, drawing 160 submissions, many of which imagined a swimming facility that doubled as a place for relaxation and community.Architecturally, the building reads as a cluster of five brick towers rising from a transparent, glazed base. Each tower takes its form from the pool positioned beneath it, giving every interior its own character while producing an irregular, stepped roofline across the skyline. Around 300,000 handmade bricks went into the towers, a tactile counterpoint to the lighter glass level below, where large windows open up harbour views and draw daylight deep inside. The standout moment sits between those towers: the Valley Pool, an outdoor basin on the first floor that lets swimmers do laps beneath an open sky, joined on the same level by an outdoor onsen-style pool looking out across the harbour.Inside, the program is organized by level and purpose. The ground floor houses a 25-metre fitness pool, a teaching pool and three play pools for children, while the upper level adds a therapy pool, a hot pool, a cold plunge and the two open-air pools. Rounding out the wellness offer are three saunas, a steam bath and a heated stone. Developed by the Paper Island Water Culture House Foundation together with the City of Copenhagen and backed by the Nordea Foundation, KAI is part of a broader push to turn the city’s harbour into a space for public recreation and culture.The building opens on December 5, 2026, with dedicated swimming and dipping zones along a timber boardwalk, facing the Royal Danish Playhouse and Opera Park, slated to follow in early 2027.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: John Goldberger’s ‘100 Superlative Rolex Watches’ Returns in a Fully Revised Edition
Art & Culture.text: SummaryJohn Goldberger’s 100 Superlative Rolex Watches returns in a fully revised edition.New photography and updated research spotlight 100 of the rarest Rolex references.Physical copies will hit European stores in December, followed by the rest of the world in Spring 2027.Nearly two decades after its original 2008 debut helped establish the modern blueprint for vintage Rolex scholarship, Damiani Books is releasing a completely revised edition of John Goldberger’s landmark reference volume, 100 Superlative Rolex Watches.Featuring an introduction by Giampiero Negretti, the updated 280-page edition brings together 100 of the rarest and most historically significant Rolex timepieces ever produced, spanning early Oyster models, cloisonné enamel dials, and military-issue Submariners to complicated moonphases and Paul Newman Cosmograph Daytonas. Developed in collaboration with some of the world's foremost collectors, the volume pairs newly commissioned high-resolution photography with updated archival research and previously unseen historical material, examining why vintage Rolex continues to serve as the benchmark at the intersection of luxury, design, and collectibility.Printed in Italy , the new edition runs to 280 pages and comes as an eco-leather hardcover with a slipcase, measuring 24.2 by 28.5 cm. It's available to order from Damiani Books, retailing at €240 EUR (approx. $265 USD). Physical copies will officially arrive in European bookstores starting December 1, 2026, followed by a wider release across the US and worldwide in Spring 2027.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
